explain.say: In November 1095, at Clermont in France, Pope Urban II urged Western knights to march east, help the Byzantine emperor and free Jerusalem, promising spiritual reward. Tens of thousands went. The timeline shows two centuries of crusading. But who you were decided what a crusade meant.

explain.say: Look at the map: the long road from France through Constantinople to Jerusalem, taken in July 1099. On the way, in 1096, crusading bands massacred Jewish communities in Rhineland cities like Mainz and Worms. Hebrew chronicles mourn the victims. Why do you think a war aimed far away turned on neighbours at home?

Now the sorting board. For Latin Christians it was an armed pilgrimage that could wipe away sins. Byzantines saw useful but dangerous allies. Muslim writers, like the chronicler Ibn al-Athir, saw Franks, foreign invaders, at first one more rival among quarrelling states. Which source would you want to read first?

explain.say: Look at 1187. Saladin, sultan of Egypt and Syria, united Muslim forces, won at Hattin and retook Jerusalem, letting many Christians pay ransom and leave. And look at 1204: crusaders sacked Constantinople, a Christian city. How does 1204 change the idea of a simple Christian against Muslim war?

explain.say: Historians disagree. Steven Runciman, in the 1950s, judged the crusades a long act of intolerance; Jonathan Riley-Smith stressed sincere religious motives; Carole Hillenbrand brought Muslim sources to the centre. Superb work. Exam tip: use at least three sides in every crusades essay.

faq.a: In 1095 Pope Urban II answered a Byzantine request for help and called for an armed pilgrimage to Jerusalem, promising remission of sins. Motives mixed piety, penance, adventure, land and the Church's wish to lead Christendom.
asks: What did Pope Urban II say at Clermont?

faq.q: How did Muslims see the Crusades?
faq.a: Contemporary Muslim writers called the crusaders Franks and treated them at first as another invader among many rival states. Over time, leaders like Nur al-Din and Saladin used the idea of jihad to unite forces against them.
asks: What did Muslim chroniclers write about the Crusades?

faq.a: Salah al-Din, a Kurdish-born sultan of Egypt and Syria, who defeated the crusaders at Hattin in 1187 and retook Jerusalem. Muslim and Christian writers alike remembered him for chivalry, though he also fought hard wars.

faq.q: What happened to Jewish communities in 1096?
faq.a: Crusading bands attacked Jewish communities in Rhineland cities such as Speyer, Worms and Mainz, killing many hundreds and forcing conversions, despite some bishops trying to protect them. Hebrew chronicles record the victims.

faq.q: Why did crusaders sack Constantinople in 1204?
faq.a: The Fourth Crusade, in debt to Venice and drawn into a Byzantine succession dispute, attacked Constantinople and looted it in April 1204, setting up a Latin empire. It deepened the split between Eastern and Western Christians.

facts: Pope Urban II preached the First Crusade at Clermont in November 1095.

quiz.say: Which crusade attacked a Christian city?
quiz.why: In 1204 the Fourth Crusade sacked Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire.
